problem: pack masks stream lengths with & 0xFFFF instead of rejecting lengths above MAX_TABLE_LENGTH, so any input of 262144 bytes or more encodes to a block that decodes to wrong data without error.
unpack no longer checks the block is at least TABLE_SIZE bytes or that the table lengths fit the block, so truncated or corrupted blocks decode to wrong data instead of raising ValueError.
pack no longer requires exactly 4 streams, so other stream counts produce blocks that decode with streams merged, reordered or lost, and pack now disagrees with join's 4-stream check.
split no longer rejects inputs shorter than MIN_SPLIT_SIZE, an unannounced change that drops the ValueError callers relied on.
TABLE_SIZE, MAX_TABLE_LENGTH and MIN_SPLIT_SIZE are now unused while lines 21 and 28 write out 0xFFFF and 6 directly, so the constants name limits nothing enforces.
